reason: The hypothesis relies on three key premises about heterogeneous structures and glaze layers, which are directly supported by E1 and E2. However, the evidence comes from bulk CCAs, not thin-film FeNiCrCoCu coatings, so the applicability premise is an overstatement not supported by the cited passages.
premises: Heterogeneous structural evolutions (e.g., nanocomposite/amorphous tribo-layers, precipitation-reinforced interfaces, gradient nanograined subsurfaces) can elevate wear resistance in alloys.
Tribo-oxidation can form a protective glaze layer of nanocrystalline oxides that provides solid lubrication and enhances the friction interface at high temperatures.
In complex concentrated alloys (CCAs), heterogeneous structural evolutions can accelerate the formation of protective glaze layers during high-temperature wear.
The cited evidence is directly applicable to FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coatings under high-temperature sliding conditions.
